tasks.title: Railway trial D: build the trial corridor with the production line feature, ride it, judge it
tasks.notes:
GOAL. First real use of the production railway line feature: build the trial corridor in the live world, ride it end to end, and judge it with the owner. This is the representative build and the in-game judgement the code tickets cannot do.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md (all of it: what the 2026-11-22 trial found, "Owner decisions", "Ticket plan"); docs/agents/model-and-effort.md (builderTask dispatch gate; the owner must be present); rules/build-roles.md and `python3 scripts/build_roles.py --world southampton-build show`; rules/process.md; the railway line feature (lib/builds/railway_plan.py and the integration module) and its README or rules section.

PLACE: the trial corridor in world southampton-build, MC x 6740 to 7430, z -4400 to -3890 (cells 52..58, -35..-31). Ghost ground already exists for all of it. It contains one double-track main line, one double-track branch curve, one level crossing near MC 6980,-4343 (cell 54,-34), two mapped rail bridge spans (near 7285,-4290 and from 7415,-4107 to 7474,-4020), and 19 rail switches (a junction near 6820,-4085). The 2026-11-22 trial corridor was removed; the area is back to ghost ground.

DECISIONS TO HONOUR: docs/plans/railway.md "Owner decisions" 1 to 14. In particular: powered rail on every straight cell with a torch two blocks below; junctions, sidings and yards are NOT built (leave gaps for humans and report them); the line leaves gaps at the crossing and both bridges with end records (the crossing feature is built later by its own ticket); best effort, and fail loudly where a stretch cannot be made rail-legal.

STEPS:
1. Check the dispatch gate and the build roles; start under `python3 scripts/site_lock.py --world southampton-build run <owner> "<task>" -- <cmd>`. Plan with the production builder; read its failures list first. Dry-run before applying.
2. Apply, then verify by read-back (rails match the plan, every powered rail powered, torches present).
3. With the owner in the game, ride a cart end to end on each track; record where it stops or derails and why. Check corners, ascending rails, the speed on staircase stretches, the bed and slopes against the real surroundings, and the planting.
4. List the spots a human should fix (junction, the gaps at the crossing and bridges, anything that looked wrong), with coordinates. File any snags in the world repo (scripts/issues.py, the snag skill), not as tasks.
5. Write the findings into docs/plans/railway.md under a "Trial D" heading: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the footprint (should be none), minutes and session tokens used (state the method), actual models and efforts, the ride result, and the owner's in-game verdict.
6. NEXT STEP, DO NOT FILE IT YET: decor sidings, yards and spurs (best-effort decor, clean unbroken runs only, never tied into junctions). The owner chose the study area: the yard around 50.91436,-1.45871 (MC 1901,-3299, cell 23,-32; 17 sidings, 3 crossovers, 2 spurs, 20 switches, a viaduct over the rails; probe extracts in the world repo under reference/vector_map/rail_probe_complex/). Say in the findings whether the line is good enough to start it and what its brief should contain.

ACCEPTANCE: docs/plans/railway.md has a Trial D section with a Cost heading and table rows and the owner's in-game verdict; the ride result per track is recorded; the human-fix list has coordinates; nothing written outside the footprint.


Owner decisions (2026-11-23, grilling): (1) At a junction on the main line, the line is laid straight through; only the side track leaves a gap, reported with coordinates as a job for a person. (2) Pass bar for the ride: each track rides from gap to gap on straights, curves and slopes with no derailing or stall. Any other stop is a defect, listed with coordinates. A defect on the main line means 'not good enough yet' and the findings say what to fix first. Planting and bed-look defects are noted but do not fail the ride. If the ride passes, the findings say the line is ready for the decor sidings and yards step. Put both in the acceptance and in the Trial D findings.

Returned to todo: Planner refused at the footbridge near MC 6872,-4194 (no deck height evidence); waits for structure evidence (#450) and the planner hookup (#451). Worktree .worktrees/384-railway-trial-d holds no code changes. Half-done on branch task/384-railway-trial-d.

[tasks CLI] Status update recorded; subject to human review.

tasks.title: First crossing feature: the level crossing near 6980,-4343 from OSM tags and Street View
tasks.notes:
GOAL. Design and build the first level crossing feature, in game, with the owner: the crossing near MC 6980,-4343 (cell 54,-34). Claude chooses the gates, lights and colours from OSM tags and Street View, then builds it using the crossing mechanism.

READ FIRST: AGENTS.md; docs/plans/railway.md ("Owner decisions" 7, 9, 10, 11); docs/plans/bridges-and-tunnels.md ("Already decided"); docs/agents/model-and-effort.md (builderTask gate; owner present); the crossing feature module and schema from the crossing mechanism ticket (lib/builds/, rules/feature-builds.md); the `snag` skill; rules/build-roles.md.

EVIDENCE ALREADY FOUND (OSM, node on each of the two tracks about 4 blocks apart, near 50.92340 N, 1.38633 W): `railway=level_crossing`, `crossing:barrier=double_half`, `crossing:light=yes`, `crossing:bell=yes`, `crossing:activation=remote`, description "Manually Controlled Barriers monitored with Closed-Circuit Television (MCB-CCTV)". The branch line crosses a road here; read the road data for the surface and width.

DECISIONS TO HONOUR: the rail feature trumps the road; the crossing feature lays the road surface across the rails itself; gates, lights and bell exist only because the OSM tags say so (barrier double_half, light yes, bell yes); their STYLE and COLOURS come from Street View, chosen in this build, with the frame ids recorded as evidence; no default style and no separate survey. The crossing is built after both abutting line features exist and joins their recorded levels.

STEPS:
1. Check the dispatch gate and that the line features either side of the gap exist (task 384 (Railway trial D) builds them). If not, stop and report; do not build the line here.
2. Get Street View frames: `python3 shims/streetview_sample.py --world southampton-build sample --cell 54,-34` (optional `--grid` and `--yaws`; it has no dry-run flag, so before running it tell the owner the source (Google Street View thumbnails), the cell, the number of frames and that they save under instance/streetview/, and wait for a yes; see config/system-providers.json for the licence note: do not commit the frames). Read the sheet. Note the barrier arms, lamps, signs, colours, and anything the OSM tags missed.
3. Record the evidence with scripts/decision_record.py (`evidence add`, `phase add`), write the crossing spec in site/builds/, choose valid block ids for bars, posts and lamps (iron bars and the other colour variants available in this game version; check lib/blocks/block_reference.py), dry-run, apply under the site lock, read back.
4. Judge it in game with the owner: does it read as that crossing, are the colours right, does a cart pass through. Fix by editing the spec and re-applying; file snags in the world repo, not as tasks.
5. Add a short Crossing section to docs/plans/railway.md: what Street View showed, choices made and why, what looked right or wrong, cost (minutes, session tokens, method), and the owner's verdict. Say whether the same approach should be repeated for other crossings.

ACCEPTANCE: the crossing spec and its evidence record exist in the world repo; the crossing is built, read back and judged in game by the owner; the railway findings file has the Crossing section with a Cost heading and the owner's verdict.

tasks.title: Roof stairs and blocks: make the #434 feature-roof rule the default, house roofs included
tasks.notes:
Follow-up to #434 (owner decision, 2026-11-23). #434 builds its new stairs-and-blocks rule for feature roofs only, behind an opt-in spec key, so house roofs do not change. The owner also says the house roof rim rule (roof_octant.RIM_OPTIONS, #414) over-applies: stairs where full blocks belong on house roofs. This task decides, once #434 has landed and the owner has checked it in game on Papa John's, whether the same rule becomes the default for house_build roofs and for feature roofs.

Shared code: pitched_roof_states and align_stair_shapes (lib/builds/roof_geometry.py) are called from house_build.py (about lines 772, 778 and 871) and feature_build.py; roof_octant.py holds RIM_OPTIONS.

Needed: re-read #434's rule and the owner's verdict on it; apply it to house roofs (octant rim and the terrace-edge rule) and make it the default for feature roofs if the owner agrees; house_build tests and a dry run of at least one house plan and one feature roof, with stair, slab and block counts before and after. Non-builder: fixtures and dry runs, no live apply. Acceptance: tests, the dry-run counts, and the owner's in-game check on one house after a rebuild (a separate world step).

Handoff: docs/plans/roof-and-frontage-swarm.md (section "#434 scope").

From the #434 review (merged 6e01e17, 2026-11-23): two known weaknesses of the opt-in stairs "slope" rule to settle before making it the default. (1) The slope test compares the gradient component along the stair's facing with MIN_SLOPE 0.15 m/block, so a gentle roof at about 45 degrees to the grid (0.15 to 0.21 m/m, which passes the fit) has a component near 0.12 and every interior stair is levelled; compare the gradient magnitude or scale the threshold, and add a gentle rotated fixture. (2) 'Step between volumes' is checked before 'slope', so a real slope stair on a continuous roof cut by a region seam is flattened (one case on Papa John's, 6523,-4563 facing N, fitted rise 0.44 m/m); let a fitted rise win when both volumes are fitted, and add a seam fixture. Also: stairs "slope" does not require zones surface fit (only documented); consider a warning.

tasks.title: Roof edges on noisy lidar: terrace trim beside higher cells, multi and opposing drops, no backing, fallback for unfit zones (West, Kiddle)
tasks.notes:
Fix task recommended by #460 (roof edge measurement, report docs/plans/roof-edge-measurement-2026-11-23.md, owner OK 2026-11-23). Issues I-019 (pitched roofs built from full blocks: S-024, S-068, S-069, S-118) and I-048 (flat roof stairs that gain no height: S-088).

Findings (see the report for the corrected tables): on West (site/builds/west_w34391673.json) and Kiddle (w146985470.json) the largest group of full-block rises is cells with a higher same-zone neighbour, where the terrace-edge trim in roof_geometry.pitched_roof_states never fires (West 88, Kiddle 19); next, zone-step-only cells (West 49, Kiddle 12; Kiddle 43 with zones surface fit). The trim failures named in #460 (three or more drops, opposing drops, no level backing) are small (West 14, Kiddle 6). Every flat stair with no higher cell around it comes from the terrace-edge rule #309 (West 27, Kiddle 1). The surface fit and the #434 stairs "slope" rule help modestly; West zone 49 and Kiddle zone 44 do not fit (they keep raw lidar) and carry the S-118 ragged edge.

Needed, each rule with a Build fixture that proves it and before/after counts on both roofs:
1. Let the terrace trim fire beside a half-step higher same-zone cell.
2. Handle three-or-more drops and opposing drops.
3. Handle a drop with no level backing cell.
4. A fallback for zones that fail the surface fit (a looser fit, or regions from the aerial), so West 49 and Kiddle 44 get a clean surface.
Also commit the counting script #460 used (it was left in /private/tmp; the report describes its method) under scripts/ or lib/audit/ so the counts are reproducible, and make the terrace-edge rule stop placing flat stairs (I-048).

pitched_roof_states also serves house_build (house_build.py about lines 772 and 778): any rule change needs a house plan dry run and the house_build tests; keep house roofs unchanged unless the owner agrees (making roof rules the default for houses is #462). Related: #463 (rotated hip roofs).

Non-builder: fixtures and dry runs, no live apply; switching surface fit on in the world specs is a separate world step with the owner's OK. Acceptance: counts (a) and (b) on West and Kiddle at or below the targets in the #460 report's check lines, tests per rule, and the owner's in-game look at S-024, S-068, S-069, S-118 and S-088 after a rebuild (a separate world step).

Corrected targets from the merged #460 report (b7cd9b3): visible rises (total minus half-block steps, flat cells and slope-rule blocks) West 150 on the current spec, 123 with surface fit; Kiddle 37 on the current spec, 62 with surface fit. Flat stairs with no higher cell: West 27 / 20, Kiddle 1 / 0.

tasks.title: reapply_feature: a foreign in-flight journal entry is reported as this rebuild's failure
tasks.notes:
Found in the live Chaiiwala rebuild (2026-11-24, after #458 merged at 61733d5). `python3 scripts/reapply_feature.py --world southampton-build w122706795 --apply` undid the old build and the rebuild landed (journal seq 2298 build w122706795 owner reapply-82465 -> seq 2299 landed, 03:26:37Z), yet the wrapper printed "reapply w122706795: stopped during rebuild: builder left an in-flight journal entry. Undo completed; rebuild did not complete cleanly ... To re-lay it ...". The in-flight entry it saw belonged to another session: `site_recover.py status` -> "in-flight: cell 54,-34 stage feature plan railway_54_m34 owner claude since 2026-11-24T02:04:03Z".

Fix in lib/builds/feature_reapply.py: the post-rebuild in-flight check must only count journal entries for this feature's plan (and this run's owner / seq range), not any in-flight entry in the world; report another session's in-flight entry as information, not as this run's failure. Add a test with a foreign in-flight entry present while the rebuild lands cleanly (expect success), next to the existing #458 lapse tests in scripts/test_reapply_feature.py. Also update the recovery text in rules/slow-commands.md if it says otherwise.

Non-builder: fixtures only, no live apply. Acceptance: the test, and a clean success line when only a foreign entry is in flight.

tasks.title: Test suite: supported wait for a busy full suite (stop endless agent wait loops)
tasks.notes:
Agents waiting for a busy full suite wrote shell loops that never ended (some ran for days):
- `until ! pgrep -f <pattern>` matched the loop's own zsh -c command line, so it always found itself.
- `until [ ! -e .git/ai-worldbuilder-full-suite.lock ]` never ends: run_tests.py uses an advisory flock on a file that persists (it has existed since 27 Oct), so the file is never removed.

Fix:
1. Add `run_tests.py --wait [--timeout SECS]`: block on the flock itself (not just fail fast), then run; exit non-zero with a clear message after the timeout. Default timeout is bounded (e.g. 30 min).
2. Use it in ship_branch.py where it retries on "already running".
3. One line in the agent docs (docs/agents/world-and-live-commands.md slow-command section, and the ship-branch / parallel-task-wave skills): never wait on pgrep or on lock-file existence; use `--wait`.
Done when: tests cover wait-then-run and timeout, the docs line has landed, and ship_branch no longer needs its own retry loop.

tasks.title: Railway planting: write leaves in the state the game keeps (readback mismatch)
tasks.notes:
GOAL. The railway feature's planting writes leaves in a state the game re-labels, so the apply readback fails. #384 trial D, railway_54_m34 (512 box), first real apply: planned 100,826 cells, readback found 62 then 24 mismatches after two retries, all oak leaves: planned oak_leaves[persistent=true,distance=1], found oak_leaves[distance=7,persistent=true,waterlogged=false] (leaf distance is derived from nearby logs). Journal entry 2286 was left 'begun'; site_recover would roll back. No rail, torch or ground block mismatched.

FIX. lib/builds/railway_feature.py line ~260 `plan.set(x, y, z, 'oak_leaves[persistent=true,distance=1]')`: use the same leaf state every other builder uses, 'oak_leaves[persistent=true]' (see lib/layers/tree_species.py DEFAULT_LEAVES), or better a shared constant, so the readback tolerates the game's derived distance and waterlogged properties. Check how readback normalises block states (site_kit / readback compare) so the fix is the right layer: if the readback should treat derived leaf properties as equal for every builder, say so in your report but do not widen the shared readback unless it is clearly a defect.

CHECKS. A test that the railway planting state passes the same readback comparison a game-normalised leaf would (use the repo's readback/compare helper with 'oak_leaves[distance=7,persistent=true,waterlogged=false]' as the found state), and that the old distance=1 string would fail. Run the railway tests and the full suite. No live world, nothing under worlds/.
